messages:
maya: Quick check — onboarding 'open-bert-0.9' ready for serving? I pushed weights to s3://redwood-models/open-bert-0.9/weights.tar.gz but the config.json fails schema lint in CI. Tokenizer also lowercases by default which is surprising. Anyone seen this pad/eos mismatch before?

sam: I saw the lint error earlier, it flagged `pad_token` presence + `eos_as_pad: true` as invalid in our v2 schema. CI prints: `ERROR: config.json: field 'pad_token' is not allowed when eos_as_pad=true (schema v2)`

maya: hmm, the model vendor's default config sets both. Our validator used to accept that for legacy models. Did someone flip the strictness? @sam?

sam: @maya yeah we tightened the schema last week to avoid ambiguous token mappings (caused a bunch of downstream eval regressions). New rule: either explicit pad_token OR eos_as_pad fallback, not both. The lint tool now returns exit code 2 for that case.

liam: Quick workaround: remove `eos_as_pad` from config and ensure `pad_token` is set to a real token id. But watch out: tokenizer vocab_size doesn't match model embeddings if vendor used an extra sentinel. I hit that on a different layer.

maya: here's the current config snippet from the model tarball: ```json
{
  "model_name": "open-bert-0.9",
  "max_seq_len": 2048,
  "dtype": "fp16",
  "quantization": "none",
  "tokenizer": {
    "lowercase": true,
    "pad_token": "<pad>",
    "eos_token": "</s>",
    "vocab_size": 30010
  },
  "eos_as_pad": true
}
```

toni: That exact combination trips our schema. Two options: 1) update config to remove `eos_as_pad` and map pad_token to a valid id in tokenizer files; 2) add a compatibility flag to the linter temporarily: `--allow-legacy-eos-pad` so onboarding can proceed while we normalize tokens. Which do you prefer?

maya: I'd rather normalize now (option 1) so we don't carry cruft. Can someone confirm the real pad token id in the tokenizer files bundled in the tar.gz? I can update config and re-run model-compat smoke tests.

sam: I extracted tokenizer.json from the tar.gz — pad_token exists as string but no explicit id mapping file. Embedding matrix is 30011 rows though, so vocab_size mismatch is present (config says 30010). That explains some failing token-tests in QA.

liam: oh that mismatch is the real blocker. If embeddings=30011 and config.vocab_size=30010, the runtime rejects load (shape mismatch). Fix priorities: weights path -> tokenizer vocab_size -> pad/eos mapping -> schema pass.

maya: ok plan: I'll update config.json to match embeddings (30011), remove `eos_as_pad`, and explicitly set `tokenizer.pad_token_id` to the last index. Then push new tarball and trigger the onboarding workflow. I'll also add a short note in PR describing why we changed the schema fields.

toni: sounds good. For the schema/lint side I'll add a temporary rule comment in the repo: // NOTE: allow legacy eos_as_pad only if pad_token absent and vocab_size mismatch fixed. But don't add new flags unless necessary.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: onboarding job queued for model open-bert-0.9 (s3://redwood-models/open-bert-0.9/weights_updated.tar.gz) — status: queued

maya: Pushed updated tarball and config at s3://redwood-models/open-bert-0.9/weights_updated.tar.gz. Config diff I submitted in PR #832: ```diff
- "vocab_size": 30010,
- "eos_as_pad": true,
+ "vocab_size": 30011,
+ "pad_token_id": 30010
```

sam: I'll re-run the schema linter locally with the new file. If linter still complains, we can revert to adding `--allow-legacy-eos-pad` to the CLI temporarily.

liam: FYI add a tiny unit test to the onboarding checks that asserts embeddings.shape[0] == config.vocab_size. Saved me from timeouts last week.

maya: will add that test to the smoke suite. Thanks. Also pinging @toni for a quick CR on the config change when you have a minute.

toni: on it, reviewing now. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — will follow up if CI still fails. If anyone sees other token quirks (e.g., `unk_token` mapping) call it out here and we'll fold into the same PR.
